Feature name: Online Verification: Validate Link Ownership On Submit
Feature Description: Dashboard-side and bot-side. VerificationController::verify() binds the submitter to their own Discord ID, but the guid in the request body is never checked against that user or server, and the bot's set_verified() does not check either. No API key is needed to reach this: verify() is session-authenticated, so any logged-in member can submit another member's pending guid from their own browser and burn that link, forcing the victim to restart. Griefing rather than a bypass, but cheap to close.

Feature name: Online Verification: Link Ownership Check On Page Load
Feature Description: Dashboard-side. VerificationController::index() looks the link up by gid and uuid only, never by uid, so any logged-in Discord user can open another member's verification page. They cannot submit it because verify() checks auth, but the page leaks server branding and rules and it is the check that would make the submit-side fix redundant.

Feature name: Online Verification: Fix Misnamed Route Parameter
Feature Description: Dashboard-side. The route declares POST /verify/{serverId}/{guid} but the controller signature is verify($request, $serverId, $userid), so Laravel binds that segment positionally and the segment actually carries the Discord user ID. The abort_unless auth check depends on that coincidence holding. Rename the route parameter to {userId} before someone reorders or renames it and silently removes the check.

Neither side checks created_date, so a link stays usable until the 90-day cleanup job removes the row. Low risk now that the page requires a matching Discord login, but a short expiry window is cheap hygiene and reduces the value of a leaked link.

Bot-side. A new link row is created on every button press, so one member can hold several live links at once and the table grows faster than needed. Return the existing unverified link if one is still live.
Bot-side schema. The uuid column is varchar(2048) with no unique index, and the dashboard queries it by gid plus uuid on every page load. Shrink the column and add an index.

Feature name: Online Verification: Premium Lapse And Outage Fallback
Feature Description: If premium expires between the link being issued and the member opening it, index() redirects to the missing-subscription page and the member is stuck with no route in. Same if the dashboard is unreachable. Fall back to the built-in date-of-birth modal so verification keeps working.
Dashboard-side. Record opened, abandoned and completed events for the verification page so servers can see where members drop out instead of only seeing successes.
Message the member if they opened the verification page but did not finish within a set time, recovering members who would otherwise sit in the lobby indefinitely.

Feature name: Online Verification: Device Fingerprint Alt Detection
Feature Description: Complements the planned IP check by flagging when several Discord accounts verify from the same browser fingerprint, catching alts that rotate IPs or switch to mobile data to dodge an IP match.
Combine IP, VPN, fingerprint and account-age signals into a single score shown on the approval message, so staff read one number instead of four separate flags.

Feature name: Online Verification: Country And Age-Of-Majority Rules
Feature Description: Use the connection country to apply the correct local age of majority instead of one global threshold, and optionally block or flag configured regions.

Feature name: Online Verification: ID Upload On Page
Feature Description: Let members upload identity documents through the verification page instead of Discord DM attachments. Keeps sensitive images out of Discord and gives you control over retention and deletion.
Plug a document-verification provider such as Stripe Identity, Persona or Veriff into the verification page for real document checks rather than staff eyeballing a photo.
Add a selfie or liveness step so a borrowed or stolen ID photo alone is not enough to pass.
Custom domain, logo and fuller theming on top of the existing colour and image customisation, for large branded communities that want the flow to look like their own.

Feature name: Online Verification: Accessibility And Mobile Pass
Feature Description: Audit the verification page for mobile and screen-reader use, since nearly every member will open the link on a phone straight from the Discord app.

Feature name: API: Restrict The Age Lookup Endpoint
Feature Description: Bot-side, defence in depth only. The /age/get endpoint will return a fully decrypted date of birth for any user ID passed to it, but the API key is held only by the website and the sole caller is ProfileController passing the authenticated user's own ID, so nothing is exposed today. Narrow the endpoint to that case anyway so a future caller cannot widen it without noticing, and drop the FUTURE security comment in api/ages.py once done.
Autokicked members are told they can appeal but there is no mechanism behind it. Add an appeal button and a staff review queue so wrongly kicked members have a route back.
Automatically prompt a member to verify again when their stored date of birth means they have crossed 18 or 21, or after a set number of months.
Score repeat failed attempts, dates of birth that conflict across servers, and rapid retries. The cross-server date-of-birth cache already collects the raw signal.
Opt-in network where a member verified in one partnered server is automatically trusted in another, so members do not repeat the same check in every server they join.
Add a one-time-code method over email or SMS as an alternative for servers that do not want a full ID flow.
Mark ID verifications stale after a configurable number of months and request a fresh check, for communities with compliance obligations.
Detect join velocity spikes and lock the lobby automatically instead of relying on staff noticing and running the raid kick command by hand.
One command to immediately freeze all joins and verification. Emergency safety should not require a subscription, and it is a natural upsell moment for the automatic version.
Add a timed quarantine role alongside the existing log-only and kick actions, so failing a join requirement does not have to mean being kicked.
Extend the existing requirement toggles with username pattern blocklists, the Discord quarantine flag, empty-profile checks and tiered account-age thresholds.
Opt-in publishing and subscribing of bans across servers, building on the existing banwatch service.
Persistent staff notes attached to a member and shown on the approval message, so context carries between moderators and across rejoins.
Preset denial reasons plus a templated message to the member explaining what went wrong and what to do next.
A dashboard view of the pending approval queue with multi-select approve and deny, for servers processing large volumes.
Track who approved or denied what and how quickly, giving server owners accountability over their moderation team.
Re-ping staff when a verification request has been pending longer than a configured time, using the existing approval ping role.
Snapshot a server config, restore it, copy it to another server, or save it as a reusable template. Aimed at people running several servers.
A weekly or monthly summary of joins, verifications, kicks and failures posted to a channel or sent to the owner.
Drop-off rates across join, lobby, page opened and verified, so servers can see exactly where they lose members.
Break verification success rates down per invite and inviter, showing which sources bring members who actually finish verification.
Export age demographics and join history as CSV or JSON, which also strengthens the data-portability side of GDPR.
Free servers keep 30 to 90 days of history, premium keeps twelve months or more. Retention length is an honest paid axis given how aggressively the current policy prunes.
Let members see their own verification status, which servers they are verified in, and revoke it themselves. Privacy-positive and strengthens the GDPR position.

Translate member-facing messages and the verification page into the most common languages of your user base. A growth lever rather than a paywall, though custom per-server translations could be premium.
Server logo, accent colour and footer on the messages the bot sends, matching the verification page theming.
The permission notice system only fires reactively when something breaks. Re-run the audit on a schedule and warn staff before a member hits the failure.
